titulo_es: Obligación y consejo: must, have to, should
resumen: Must y have to expresan obligación («tener que»); should da consejos («debería»). En negativa cambian mucho de sentido: mustn't prohíbe, don't have to indica que no es necesario.

filas: obligación que siente quien habla, normas escritas
She has to wear a uniform.

explicacion.texto: Must y should son modales: no llevan -s en tercera persona, van seguidos de infinitivo sin to y no usan do en preguntas (Must I...? Should we...?). Have to es un verbo normal: has to, do you have to?, didn't have to.
Must no tiene pasado ni futuro: para el pasado se usa had to (I had to work yesterday) y para el futuro will have to (You'll have to wait).

items: Mustn't ≠ don't have to: You mustn't tell him (está prohibido) frente a You don't have to tell him (no hace falta, tú decides).
Should suele suavizarse con I think: I think you should see a doctor.
Para pedir consejo: What should I do?

ejemplos.traduccion: Los pasajeros deben mostrar su billete.

ejemplos.frase: I have to get up at six every day.
ejemplos.traduccion: Tengo que levantarme a las seis todos los días.

ejemplos.frase: We don't have to pay; it's free.
ejemplos.traduccion: No tenemos que pagar; es gratis.

ejemplos.frase: Did you have to wait long?

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: You mustn't come if you are busy.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: You don't have to come if you are busy.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Si no es necesario, se usa don't have to; mustn't es prohibición.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: You should to see a dentist.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Should va seguido de infinitivo sin to.

errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I had to work last weekend.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: En pasado se usa had to.

ejercicios.enunciado: Completa con la forma correcta de have to.
ejercicios.frase: My sister ___ (have to) work on Saturdays.

ejercicios.enunciado: Completa con mustn't o don't have to.
ejercicios.frase: You ___ park here. It's for ambulances only.

ejercicios.enunciado: Completa con mustn't o don't have to.
ejercicios.frase: Tomorrow is a holiday, so we ___ go to school.
ejercicios.explicacion: No es necesario: don't have to.

ejercicios.enunciado: Completa con la forma de have to en pasado.
ejercicios.frase: The flight was cancelled, so we ___ (have to) stay at a hotel.
You look tired. You ___ go to bed so late.
It's a great film. You ___ see it.
___ wear a tie at your new job?
ejercicios.explicacion: Have to forma preguntas con do.

ejercicios.frase: Next year he ___ pay more taxes.
ejercicios.explicacion: Must no tiene futuro: will have to.

ejercicios.frase: Visitors ___ feed the animals. It's dangerous.
I have to finish the report.
respuestas: I had to finish the report.
ejercicios.explicacion: El pasado de have to es had to.
Must va seguido de infinitivo sin to.

ejercicios.frase: Does she has to work tomorrow?
respuestas: Does she have to work tomorrow?

ejercicios.enunciado: Ordena las palabras para formar una pregunta.

respuestas: You don't have to take your shoes off
You don't have to take off your shoes
ejercicios.explicacion: Sujeto + don't have to + infinitivo; take off puede ir separado.
